21                SENATOR KRUEGER:   Thank you.  To 

22   explain my vote, Mr. President.

23                We haven't seen one of these 

24   residency bills for New York City workers in a 

25   while.  But for the record, I always vote against 


                                                                1077

 1   them.  Because when you do away with the 

 2   residency laws for New York City workers or any 

 3   locality's workers, it means that very 

 4   good-paying jobs are no longer going to people 

 5   who live in New York City, and they're not 

 6   spending those good-paying job salaries in the 

 7   City of New York.  

 8                So I actually think there's a strong 

 9   argument for New York City to have residency laws 

10   for its government workers, and I'll be voting 

11   no, Mr. President.  

12                Thank you.

17   Mr. President.  

18                I rise in support of this bill.  And 

19   I just want to remind people of the reason why we 

20   originally had residency laws for New York City 

21   employees.  It was to keep New York City 

22   employees in the City of New York.

23                However, it did not prevent people 

24   who were noncitizens of the City of New York for 

25   from applying for the job and getting the job, it 


                                                                1078

 1   just said that if you were offered an opportunity 

 2   to work for the city you had 90 days to relocate 

 3   to become a resident of the City of New York.  

 4   And that worked very well for a very long period 

 5   of time.  

 6                Unfortunately, over the past three 

 7   decades New York City employees have not had 

 8   their wages keep pace with the cost of inflation.  

 9   Many of them have gone many years between 

10   contract settlements.  And the reality is our 

11   municipal workforce finds it as difficult to find 

12   affordable housing in the City of New York as 

13   everybody else does.  

14                This is an opportunity for them to 

15   be able to buy a house while they work for a city 

16   that they can no longer afford to live in.  

17                I vote in favor of the bill.  

18                Thank you, Mr. President.

22   Mr. President.

25   New York City Department of Sanitation workers

 1   must have five years of service before they can 

 2   reside outside of the New York City area in a 

 3   neighboring county.

 5   required to wait five years.  All of the other 

 6   city agencies no longer have or do not have a 

 7   five-year-service requirement before they are 

 8   able to live in neighboring counties.

10   in New York City has increased significantly and 

11   it's hard for many of these workers to own their 

12   own home and to live in the area.  So we provide 

13   the sanitation workers with the same ability to 

14   live in neighboring counties like we do for all 

15   of the other city agencies.  

16                I will vote aye.  Thank you.

24   there.

10   housing in New York City and other places.

12   just get rid of all requirements of residency, 

13   because you're only going to make the problem

15   will run looking for this elusive affordable

24   market that we find ourselves in, which is 

25   hurtful to business communities, hurtful to every 


                                                                1082

 1   community.
